text:
maria: RFC follow-up — quick proposal for a lightweight 'precision-proxy' layer to reduce customer-visible profile explosion. TL;DR: expose a small set of stable high-level profiles (e.g. 'high', 'balanced', 'low') that map internally to runtime precision combinations (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit) + deterministic fallback rules. Goal: make surface area manageable while keeping runtime flexibility for cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.

jack: sounds promising. how would a client request this? header, param, or part of the existing precision_profile field?

maria: keep it simple — reuse `precision_profile` as the public name but allow values like `proxy:balanced`. Runtime resolves that to a small rulebook in the config service. Customers see stable aliases; we can change internal mappings without breaking them.

sasha: +1. important: each mapping must be backed by shadow evals before we flip it live. we should provide a `shadow-eval` toggle per mapping so we can detect quality regressions automatically.

kim: ops question — if runtime picks between fp8/int8/4bit dynamically, how do we report billing and cost? need clear token-level attribution and a canonical mapping for invoices.

maria: plan: runtime emits telemetry tags for each response, e.g. `quant_variant=fp8-hybrid` and `degrade_score=0.023`. billing will use a canonicalized mapping layer to bucket cost (we keep canonical label separate from internal variant tag). also add a per-request `cost_hint` field for heuristics.

jack: what about fallback rules for long contexts or OOM? we can't rely on a single mapping to be correct for all shapes.

maria: agreed. sketch of a mapping + fallback example (prototype YAML):

```yaml
profile: proxy-balanced
mapping:
  - condition: "seq_len <= 2048 and input_type == 'chat'"
    variant: fp8
  - condition: "seq_len > 2048"
    variant: int8
fallbacks:
  - on_quality_drop:
      switch_to: baseline-fp16
      threshold: 0.05
  - on_oom:
      switch_to: int4-safe
```

This lets the runtime pick an optimized path but fall back to safe baselines on either quality or resource signals.

sasha: we need to standardize the quality signal (what is `degrade_score`/`on_quality_drop` semantics). recommend: deg_score = 1 - BLEU-ish top-1 agreement on a fixed prompt set over a sliding window; thresholding + hysteresis to avoid flip-flops. Add a shadow bucket to collect higher fidelity metrics.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary mapping `precision-proxy:v0.1` deployed to prod-canary (t=1765433280).

kim: ok. I'll need the schema to add billing mapping and a lint rule to prevent ambiguous conditions (e.g., overlapping conditions without explicit priority). also add a migration guard for existing customer overrides.

maria: action items: 1) I will own a prototype PR for the config schema + runtime resolver (this week). 2) @sasha will wire up shadow-eval harness and smoke tests. 3) @kim will add billing canonicalization + lint.

jack: :thumbsup: should we file a short RFC addendum or just a follow-up note on the precision-profile RFC?

maria: I'll open a short RFC addendum linking back to the main precision-profile RFC and include the YAML samples, telemetry keys, and canary plan.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary progress=50% at 1765433295.

sasha: for the smoke test, add top-k overlap, perplexity on a small heldout anchored set, and a token-level delta histogram. prefer small, fast checks for canaries.

maria: agreed. thanks all — I'll post the PR link here once created and schedule a 30-min sync after the prototype lands. :sparkles:

jack: thanks — excited to see if this trims complexity without sacrificing user-facing control.

maria: quick note: this is intended to be opt-in for customers initially; we'll keep the legacy detailed profiles available until we validate.

kim: SGTM — I'll put the billing & lint TODOs into a ticket and sync with @maria later today.

ops-bot: noted: ticket created for billing mapping (ops-7892).

maria: closing loop — will update thread with PR + canary metrics.
